tables.description: Census 2023’s count of enumerated structures — 24 kinds, from schools and hospitals to factories, mosques and police stations — by district and tehsil.
tables.notes: The only table here that covers the whole frame Data Darbar draws: 156 districts and 649 tehsils, every district of Azad Jammu & Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan included. tables.description: Population and Housing Census 2017 unit tables: 35 of 40 tables at district, tehsil, sub-tehsil and sub-division level.
tables.notes: Do not sum across unit_type, locality or sex — each is a nested hierarchy and adding the levels together double- or triple-counts. Many indicators are RATES or PERCENTAGES (literacy, sex ratio, growth) and must never be summed; read the indicator label before aggregating. missing = TRUE marks a cell PBS printed as a dash; in this panel 899,800 of those 901,438 rows carry a recovered value of 0, read back from the combined district PDFs, so the zero is real rather than absent — unlike 2023, where a dash is left NULL. series_ambiguous = TRUE on 31,963 rows flags a series whose key is not unique within its table, so a filter on indicator and col_label alone may return more than one series there. Tables 23–26 are the individual-locality tables and are not in this panel. Comparing to census_panel_2023 by table_id or indicator is unsafe: the numbering differs and only 50 indicator labels match verbatim.

tables.name: census_unit_map
tables.description: One row per census unit saying which PBS 2023 shape it is drawn on, and — where that is not a straight match — why.
tables.notes: This is the crosswalk turned into a decision. A crosswalk says what happened to a unit; this says what a figure for it means when drawn on the 2023 frame. comparable is the field to read: yes where the figure belongs on the shape as published; combined where two 2017 units share one 2023 shape and must be added, or averaged on weight for a rate; parent where a unit was split and its figure is drawn across every successor at once rather than divided between them; flagged where the district persists but its territory changed; no where nothing can honestly be drawn. map_key can therefore name several shapes, space-separated. Anything that totals or ranks must count units and not shapes: a parent drawn across its successors is visited once per shape, which turns a national total of 207,684,626 into 213.4 million.
tables.source: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics, Population and Housing Censuses 2017 and 2023 and the Digital Census 2023 layer; derived from the 2017→2023 crosswalks

tables.name: climate_events
tables.description: Flood, drought and cyclone events affecting Pakistan, 2001 to 2025.
tables.notes: 31 events: 23 floods, 4 droughts, 4 tropical cyclones. An event is a named episode with a start and end, and date_precision says how well the dates are known. These events do NOT join to climate_impacts: the impact records carry no event key, only their own report_id, so the two are separate universes and attributing an impact row to an event here would be an inference, not a lookup. An earlier note said climate_impacts carries what each one did, which invited a join that cannot be made.

tables.description: Impacts reported by disaster reporting: people affected, killed, displaced, and assets damaged, by place and reporting period.

There is no event key in this table and none that joins to climate_events, so an impact cannot be attributed to a named event by lookup - only by reading the period and the place, which is an inference. The metric column says what is counted and the figures come from whichever report covered that place, so coverage is uneven between places and between periods. Do not read a missing row as a zero.

tables.name: crops_district_fy
tables.description: Area, production and yield by crop, district and fiscal year, 1981–82 to 2024–25.
tables.notes: 108 crops over 123 districts and 44 fiscal years. All 123 district codes join the PBS 2023 layer exactly, but the frame is older than that layer: 33 of the 156 districts Data Darbar draws have no crop rows at all — every district of Azad Jammu & Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan, which have their own agricultural authorities, six of Karachi’s seven, and the most recently created districts (Chaman, Duki, Surab, Sohbatpur, Upper Chitral, Upper and Lower Kohistan, Keamari). Karachi appears once, under Karachi Central’s code, and is vestigial rather than city-wide: six crops and nothing at all in recent years. Two crops are unlabelled on PBS’s portal and are carried as ‘Unnamed crop (portal id 124/125)’ rather than dropped — 125 is not small, at 85,000 hectares in 2024–25. Coverage varies by crop: the majors run from 1981–82, most vegetables and fruit from 2008–09.

tables.source: PBS Agriculture Statistics via the national accounts portal, pull of 2026-09-27

tables.name: district_crosswalk_2017_2023
tables.description: Every district-level relationship between Census 2017 and Census 2023, as groups that cover the same ground.
tables.notes: A group is the smallest set of 2017 and 2023 units covering the same territory, so a merge has two 2017 units and one 2023 unit and a split has one and several. All 127 groups balance. A group that did not would mean the relation asserted for it is wrong.

tables.name: district_indicators
tables.description: Every district-level indicator in Data Darbar, one row per district × indicator × year.
tables.notes: Long format so heterogeneous sources share one table. Filter `kind = 'indicator'` for the measures themselves; kind='quality' rows carry the sample size and small-n flag for the same prefix, and kind='provenance' rows record borrowed estimates. Survey groups suppress cells with n<30 upstream, so an absent row can mean 'suppressed' as well as 'not collected'. DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAP: where a district was split after Census 2017 (see the *_boundary_change provenance rows) both halves carry the SAME 2017 figure for the combined pre-split area, so summing a 2017 count across all districts overstates the total. Filter those rows out, or sum the 2023 year instead. Census education source corrections dated 2026-09-25 use original PBS Table 15 (2017) and Table 13 (2023); see the website methodology. Missing source counts are unavailable, not zero.
tables.source: PBS Census 2017 & 2023, Economic Census 2023, PSLM 2019-20, LFS 2020-21/2024-25, HIES 2024-25; PDHS 2017-18 (NIPS and ICF); MICS district rounds (Punjab 2017-18, Sindh 2018-19, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa 2019, Balochistan 2019-20, Gilgit-Baltistan 2016-17, Azad Jammu & Kashmir 2020-21; the provincial and regional bureaus of statistics and planning departments, with UNICEF)

tables.name: mouza_tehsil

tables.notes: Every column is a COUNT OF MOUZAS (revenue villages), never of people or households — a mouza of 12,000 and a mouza of 300 each count once. tables.description: The macro time-series panel: every observation of every SBP series held here.
tables.notes: One row per series × date. Frequencies are mixed, so filter on the catalogue's `frequency` before resampling or averaging across series. DOUBLE-COUNTING TRAP (country-wise remittances, TS_GP_BOP_WR_M): the country series are hierarchical, so summing them all overstates the total by ~42% (FY2024-25: 54,384 vs the published 38,299 Mn USD). 'U.A.E.' already contains Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah and 'Other four U.A.E.'s States'; 'Other GCC Countries excluding Saudi Arabia & U.A.E.' already contains Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman and Qatar; 'ten European Countries' already contains Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherland, Spain and Sweden — Norway and Switzerland are reported separately. The partition that reconciles exactly to the published total is: Saudi Arabia, U.A.E., U.K., U.S.A., Other GCC, ten European Countries, Norway, Switzerland, Australia, Canada, Japan, Malaysia, South Africa, South Korea, Other Countries. The same shape applies to province-wise banking (TS_GP_BAM_ADVDEP_HY), where 'all Pakistan' is the total of the regional series.

tables.name: school_access_district
tables.description: Distance to the nearest government school by sex, enrolment by sex, and school counts, one row per district (132).
tables.notes: all_km, boys_km, girls_km are POPULATION-WEIGHTED MEDIAN straight-line distances (Lambert conformal conic, km) from every populated 1 km cell to the nearest school of that network; *_min are walking minutes on the Malaria Atlas friction surface. gap_km = girls_km − boys_km (positive = girls further). Networks are by name designation; for Sindh the same medians under the attendance and girls-or-mixed definitions are in girls_km_attend / girls_km_mixed (the designation gap of 0.8 km falls to zero under attendance). tt_caveat flags districts where the friction surface is unreliable (GB) or mountain/desert cells make minutes an upper bound. *_in_school_pct_5_16 are Census 2023 Table 13(b) enrolment rates (enrolled / population aged 5–16) with successor districts summed into parents, so 123 of the 132 rows carry them. living_standards_deprivation_pslm is the (censored) MPI component; material_deprivation_pslm is an uncensored index from PSLM 2019-20 (no toilet, no flush, no piped water, food insecurity). *_n_schools count schools whose POINT falls in the district polygon (the basis of the piece's Figure 1); schools_listed / _with_coords / _in_analysis count rows by the SOURCE's district. The two bases differ where geocoded points cross a boundary. Distances depend on the whole network, not the district's own schools, so a district with few schools can still be close to the next district's.

tables.name: school_validation_district
tables.description: External-validity test of the school layer against the Mouza Census 2020, one row per mouza district (147): count floors and village-reported distances.
tables.notes: The Mouza Census asked every rural mouza whether an institution for boys and one for girls exists at each level and, if not, how far the nearest is. It is sector-blind and counts villages, so it cannot audit the layer line by line; it puts a FLOOR under the count (a village with one has at least one) and gives an INDEPENDENT distance. ratio_* = schools in the layer ÷ mouzas reporting an institution of that sex and level: well under 1 means schools are missing or misclassified; above 1 is expected. The floor test is diagnostic only where private and co-educational provision is scarce — at primary level in Punjab a low ratio is private schools, and in Sindh 'girls undercounted relative to boys' fires by construction because designated boys' schools include the Mixed majority. status = 'absent from harvest' marks the 15 mouza districts the layer does not cover (7 merged districts, 8 AJK). village_* columns are means and medians of the villages' reported km; model_* are the layer's population-weighted medians and shares; *_gap_* are girls minus boys. Compare ranks and signs, not levels: village distances are unweighted, by road, any sector. Run on the released table (in_analysis rows), so these figures describe schools_pk, not the raw registers.

tables.notes: Punjab coordinates updated on 30 September 2026: 37,917 of 38,149 current roster schools link by inferred EMIS convention to the 2017 public-school point layer linked by Pakistan Institute of Education. examples.title: Ten poorest districts
examples.sql:
SELECT rank, name, prov, mpi, H, A
FROM mpi_districts
WHERE low_n = 0   -- drop districts whose sample is too small to rank
ORDER BY rank LIMIT 10;

examples.title: Female literacy, 2017 vs 2023
examples.sql:
SELECT district, province,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2017') AS lit_2017,
       max(value) FILTER (year = '2023') AS lit_2023,
       round(max(value) FILTER (year = '2023')
           - max(value) FILTER (year = '2017'), 1) AS change
FROM district_indicators
WHERE indicator = 'literacy_ratio_female'
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY change DESC;

examples.title: Urbanisation vs multidimensional poverty
examples.sql:
SELECT d.district, d.province, d.value AS pct_urban_2023, m.mpi
FROM district_indicators d
JOIN mpi_districts m USING (district_key)
WHERE d.indicator = 'urban_proportion' AND d.year = '2023'
  AND m.low_n = 0
ORDER BY m.mpi DESC;

examples.title: What Pakistan exports most, FY2024-25
examples.sql:
-- country IS NULL rows are the commodity totals; country rows are the
-- partner split of the same money. Never add both.
SELECT hs8, any_value(commodity) AS commodity,
       round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'export' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY rs_bn DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Top import partners, FY2024-25 (Rs bn)
examples.sql:
SELECT country, round(sum(fy_value_kpkr) / 1e6, 1) AS rs_bn
FROM trade_hs8
WHERE direction = 'import' AND fiscal_year = '2024-25'
  AND country IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY rs_bn DESC LIMIT 15;

examples.title: Real GDP growth by year
examples.sql:
SELECT year, round(value, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM national_accounts
WHERE table_sheet = 'Table 6' AND item LIKE 'D GDP%'
ORDER BY year;

examples.title: Federal defence budget over time
examples.sql:
-- is_own_year_be keeps the document's own-year budget estimate,
-- the only column that strings into a clean time series.
SELECT doc_fy, item, value_rs_mn
FROM budget_lines
WHERE is_own_year_be AND item ILIKE '%defence%'
ORDER BY doc_fy;

examples.title: Rural electrification, worst tehsils (Mouza Census)
examples.sql:
-- Shares are of MOUZAS, not people. Aggregate to the polygon first:
-- several PBS tehsils can share one boundary.
SELECT x.dd_name AS tehsil, m.province,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS no_electricity,
       sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
         + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas") AS base,
       round(100.0 * sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas")
             / nullif(sum(m."ElectrictiyAvailability_AllMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_MostlyMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_SomeMouzas"
               + m."ElectrictiyAvailability_NoneMouzas"), 0), 1) AS pct_dark
FROM mouza_tehsil m
JOIN mouza_crosswalk x USING (tehsil_code)
WHERE m.TotalMauzaCount > 0
GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING base >= 50
ORDER BY pct_dark DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Girls' middle-plus schools by district (Figure 1 of the girls' school piece)
examples.sql:
-- Count by the polygon the point falls in (analysis_district_key_boundary), which is
-- how the piece counts; district_key is the register's own district.
SELECT analysis_district_key_boundary AS district,
       count(*) FILTER (analysis_sex = 'G') AS girls_schools,
       count(*) FILTER (analysis_sex = 'B') AS boys_schools
FROM schools_pk
WHERE in_analysis AND middle_plus AND analysis_district_key_boundary IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY girls_schools DESC;

examples.title: How precise are the positions, by province?
examples.sql:
-- Never map Punjab's tehsil-centroid rows as if they were GPS fixes.
SELECT province, coord_precision, count(*) AS schools,
       round(100.0 * count(*) / sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY province), 1) AS pct
FROM schools_pk
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY province, schools DESC;

examples.title: Sindh: designated boys' schools that enrol girls
examples.sql:
-- In Sindh the name says GB (boys) but SEMIS calls most of them Mixed and the
-- roster shows girls enrolled. This is why the piece reports the Sindh gap
-- under three network definitions.
SELECT district, count(*) AS boys_designated,
       count(*) FILTER (gender_official = 'Mixed') AS officially_mixed,
       count(*) FILTER (girls_enrolled > 0) AS enrolling_girls,
       sum(girls_enrolled) AS girls_in_them
FROM schools_pk
WHERE province = 'Sindh' AND gender = 'Boys' AND functional AND middle_plus
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY girls_in_them DESC;

examples.title: Where girls are furthest from a middle school, and how many are in school
examples.sql:
SELECT district, region, girls_middle_median_km, boys_middle_median_km, gap_km,
       girls_in_school_pct_5_16, boys_in_school_pct_5_16, tt_caveat
FROM school_access_district
ORDER BY girls_middle_median_km DESC LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Does the Mouza Census agree? Districts where the layer fails its floor test
examples.sql:
-- ratio < 1 means fewer schools in the layer than villages reporting one:
-- schools are missing or misclassified. Sindh's girls-v-boys flag fires by
-- construction (see the notes); read the girls' ratio itself.
SELECT region, mouza_district, ratio_midplus_G, ratio_midplus_B, ratio_high_G, flag
FROM school_validation_district
WHERE status = 'matched' AND ratio_midplus_G < 0.9
ORDER BY ratio_midplus_G;

examples.title: Tehsils where girls are furthest from a middle school
examples.sql:
-- Distances depend on the whole region's network, not the tehsil's own
-- schools; Punjab rows are geocoded, so compare them at district scale.
SELECT tehsil, district_key, region, girls_middle_km, boys_middle_km, gap_middle_km,
       girls_middle_schools, girls_middle_over5km_pct
FROM school_access_tehsil
WHERE coord_tier = 'A'   -- GPS-quality positions only
ORDER BY girls_middle_km DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Sindh multilateration: solved positions that disagree with the RSU pin
examples.sql:
-- 24% of RSU pins sit more than 300 m from the position solved from SELD's own
-- distance checker; the table keeps both so the choice can be audited.
SELECT district, name, level, coord_method, coord_resid_m, pin_vs_solved_m, lat, lng
FROM schools_pk
WHERE province = 'Sindh' AND pin_vs_solved_m > 5000
ORDER BY pin_vs_solved_m DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Travel time to care by poverty quintile
examples.sql:
-- Districts in fifths by MPI (equal numbers of districts), each fifth weighted by
-- population. The piece's 47 v 5 minutes uses population quintiles and medians;
-- the gradient is the same either way.
WITH q AS (
  SELECT h.*, ntile(5) OVER (ORDER BY m.mpi) AS mpi_quintile
  FROM health_access_district h JOIN mpi_districts m USING (district_key)
  WHERE m.low_n = 0)
SELECT mpi_quintile, count(*) AS districts,
       round(sum(mot_popw_mean * pop_2020) / sum(pop_2020), 1) AS motorised_min,
       round(sum(wal_popw_mean * pop_2020) / sum(pop_2020), 1) AS walking_min,
       round(sum(mot_pct_pop_gt60 * pop_2020) / sum(pop_2020), 1) AS pct_over_60_min_motorised
FROM q GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

examples.title: Tehsils where most people are over an hour from care even with a vehicle
examples.sql:
SELECT tehsil, district_key, province, pop_2020, mot_popw_mean, mot_pct_pop_gt60, wal_pct_pop_gt120
FROM health_access_tehsil
WHERE mot_pct_pop_gt60 > 50
ORDER BY pop_2020 DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Find a State Bank series by name
examples.sql:
-- sbp_observations is one row per series x date. Start here: find the
-- series, note its unit and frequency, then join on series_key.
SELECT series_key, series_name, unit, frequency, available_since, available_upto
FROM sbp_series_catalog
WHERE series_name ILIKE '%remittance%'
ORDER BY dataset_code, series_key;

examples.title: The rupee against the dollar since 1947
examples.sql:
SELECT o.obs_date, o.value AS pkr_per_usd
FROM sbp_observations o
JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_ER_FAERPKR_M'   -- bank floating average rates, monthly
  AND c.series_name = 'Average Exchange rate of Pak Rupees per U.S. Dollar'
  -- (a sibling series, 'App (+) / Dep (-) ...', holds the monthly % change)
ORDER BY o.obs_date;

examples.title: Where remittances come from, FY2024-25
examples.sql:
-- The country series are hierarchical (U.A.E. contains Dubai/Abu Dhabi/Sharjah,
-- 'Other GCC' contains Bahrain/Kuwait/Oman/Qatar, 'ten European Countries'
-- contains Belgium..Sweden). Summing all of them overstates the total by 42%;
-- these fifteen add up exactly to SBP's published figure.
SELECT replace(c.series_name, 'Workers'' remittances received from ', '') AS source,
       round(sum(o.value)) AS mn_usd
FROM sbp_observations o JOIN sbp_series_catalog c USING (series_key)
WHERE c.dataset_code = 'TS_GP_BOP_WR_M'
  AND o.obs_date BETWEEN DATE '2024-07-01' AND DATE '2025-06-30'
  AND replace(c.series_name, 'Workers'' remittances received from ', '') IN (
    'Saudi Arabia', 'U.A.E.', 'U.K.', 'U.S.A.',
    'Other GCC Countries excluding Saudi Arabia & U.A.E.', 'ten European Countries',
    'Norway', 'Switzerland', 'Australia', 'Canada', 'Japan', 'Malaysia',
    'South Africa', 'South Korea', 'Other Countries')
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY mn_usd DESC;

examples.title: Census 2023 population by district — the safe filter
examples.sql:
-- The panel nests levels: district rows and the tehsil rows inside them both
-- exist, and locality sums to its own total, so pin both.
-- Then watch the sex column. In tables 1, 3, 21 and 25 the sex split is
-- carried in the INDICATOR label while sex stays 'all', so sex = 'all' here
-- would still hand back the male, female and transgender rows. Name the
-- indicator exactly; ILIKE '%POPULATION%' also catches POPULATION 2017.
SELECT province_area, unit AS district, value AS population
FROM census_panel_2023
WHERE table_id = '1' AND unit_type = 'district'
  AND indicator = 'POPULATION-2023 / ALL SEXES'
  AND locality = 'all' AND NOT missing
ORDER BY population DESC;
-- 136 rows adding to 241,499,431 — PBS's published national total.

examples.title: Check a filter before you trust it
examples.sql:
-- Worth doing on any table_id you have not used before: if a single unit
-- returns more than one row, your filter is not yet a series.
SELECT indicator, col_label, locality, sex, count(*) AS rows_, sum(value) AS total
FROM census_panel_2023
WHERE table_id = '1' AND unit = 'LAHORE DISTRICT'
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4
ORDER BY rows_ DESC, total DESC
LIMIT 20;

examples.title: Tehsil populations joined to the map geometry
examples.sql:
-- dd_id is the key the site's tehsil layer uses. It is NULL on district rows
-- and missing for about 150,000 tehsil rows, so an inner join silently drops
-- units; count what you lose before mapping.
SELECT count(*) AS tehsil_rows,
       count(dd_id) AS joinable_to_geometry,
       count(*) - count(dd_id) AS would_be_dropped
FROM census_panel_2023
WHERE table_id = '1' AND unit_type = 'tehsil'
  AND locality = 'all' AND sex = 'all' AND indicator ILIKE '%POPULATION%';

examples.title: Why 2017 and 2023 cannot simply be joined
examples.sql:
-- Both panels use the same column names, which makes a cross-year join look
-- easy. It is not: the indicator vocabularies barely overlap, and most of the
-- difference is punctuation rather than meaning. Until a crosswalk exists,
-- read this before comparing anything across the two censuses.
WITH a AS (SELECT DISTINCT indicator FROM census_panel_2017),
     b AS (SELECT DISTINCT indicator FROM census_panel_2023)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM a) AS labels_2017,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM b) AS labels_2023,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM a SEMI JOIN b USING (indicator)) AS identical_labels;

examples.title: A dash means different things in the two panels
examples.sql:
-- 2017 recovered its dashes from the printed PDFs and stored them as a real 0;
-- 2023 left them NULL. So a count of populated cells is not comparable across
-- the years, and neither is an average taken over missing rows.
SELECT 2017 AS census_year, missing, count(*) AS rows_, count(value) AS with_a_value
FROM census_panel_2017 GROUP BY 1, 2
UNION ALL
SELECT 2023, missing, count(*), count(value)
FROM census_panel_2023 GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY census_year, missing;
